_note: Input to tools/build-reading.mjs. Chapter 9, graded reading.
This file pins card ids and nothing else that matters. Every safety fact
below is re-derived from Aozora's own bibliography CSV on every run, so a
wrong note here fails the build instead of shipping. What this file really
carries is the two judgments a machine cannot make: which stories a person
has read, and which ones are held back.
Why an allowlist and not a top-N by kana ratio: the research measured all
413 dual-jurisdiction-safe children's works and found that one title in the
safe set is a slur in modern Japanese. An automatic selection would have
Aozora publishes several of these stories twice, once in the pre-1946
orthography, which is why filters.orthography exists and is asserted per
story rather than assumed from the card id.

index.name: Aozora Bunko bibliography, all works by contributor, extended, UTF-8

why: orthography: the pre-1946 editions spell the geminate with a full-size kana and use kana that no reader has met since the reform. A beginner meeting them learns a spelling that is wrong today.
copyright_flag: Aozora's own determination that the work is out of copyright in Japan.

death_year_at_or_before: a work whose every contributor was dead by 1945 was already out of copyright in Japan on 1996-01-01, so the URAA restored nothing and it is public domain in the US too. This is the repository's computation, not Aozora's.

ruby_rule.counted_as: distinct word and reading pairs, not occurrences
why: A typed rung draws its items from #ruby. Counting occurrences lets one word repeated sixteen times look like sixteen items, and the round then asks the same question every turn.
tools/validate-corpus.mjs enforces this against any chapter exercise whose items pointer ends in #ruby.

an acolyte forgets his sutra, sings a rabbit's song in its place and is fed a bun for it. Buddhist practice is the setting, not the subject.
the sutra and the song are set as indented blocks in the source. The generator joins each block into one unit so the drills do not fill with one-word sentences.

why: This is not the story-4 the plan named. The plan pinned card 4674 and this file ships card 4677 in its place, for two reasons that were both measured on 2026-09-08 and neither of which a builder can fix inside workstream C's files.

First, card 4674 carries eighteen ruby occurrences but only three distinct word and reading pairs, and sixteen of the eighteen are the same word. The plan chose it on the count of eighteen. A typed rung over three items is not the drill the rung was written for.

Second, card 4674's text contains, as an ordinary noun, the single character that is also the title of a 1941 song banned by CONTRACTS C11.4. tools/check-licence.mjs fails on that character anywhere under data/, and its ALLOW_SEA list is the sanctioned way to permit an occurrence. That file belongs to no workstream in this plan, so extending it is a decision for the integration lead and not a change workstream C may make.

Card 4677 is the highest-kana story on the research's ladder that clears the eight distinct ruby entries the plan's own rule asks for, contains no banned string, and is by the same author under the same card conditions.

To go back to card 4674: set build true on the held entry below, set build false here, and add its noun phrase to ALLOW_SEA in tools/check-licence.mjs with a comment naming this story. The three-item typed rung remains a separate problem.
